clue.text: Group see gold and copper beginning to soar

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the letter C is pronounced like the word see
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the opening letter of soar

explanation.surface: A party group is told that gold and copper prices are starting to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: The chemical symbols do most of the work; 'see' stands for the letter that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a closed meeting or faction of a political party, i.e. a group of members.

clue.text: Diplomatic official cheers up, overlooking facial feature

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top
in a down entry, one piece overlooking another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers
tache is short for moustache

explanation.surface: An embassy official brightens up, ignoring something about someone's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers up' reads like brightening; it is a thank-you word turned upside down. 'Overlooking' seems to mean ignoring but here means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a junior diplomat attached to an embassy, often with a specialist brief.

clue.text: Coin slots adapted for new arrivals

indicators.note: something adapted is changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Vending machines get their coin slots modified for newcomers to the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonists are settlers newly arrived in a territory they have come to occupy.

clue.text: Snap goal attempt

blocks.note: first meaning: a photograph
second meaning: a kick or strike at goal

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a quick shot at goal; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a photograph and an attempt to score in football or hockey.

clue.text: Give detailed account of Beatrix (cheery) regularly on return

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept
returning means going back the way you came, so the kept letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Someone recounts in detail how cheerful Beatrix was when she got back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to narrate or list facts at length, giving a full account.

clue.text: Silly dunderhead, no use at first, caught thus?

indicators.note: having no of something means it is taken away from the word
silly suggests muddled, so the remaining letters are jumbled
'at first' keeps only the first letter of 'use'

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of use, which is removed

explanation.surface: A foolish idiot, failing at first, is caught in the act.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition describes how one is caught rather than giving a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught red-handed means being caught in the very act of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Not one firm in California produces powder

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the state abbreviation goes round

blocks.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
not one is none, i.e. zero, shaped like O
Co is short for company

explanation.surface: A Californian business that isn't a single firm makes some powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not one' gives zero, read as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is the powder ground from roasted cacao beans, used for drinks and baking.

clue.text: Ends 50% reduction in winter dress

indicators.note: cutting by half means the first half of the word is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written, then halved
a mini is a short dress

explanation.surface: A sale announcement: half price on winter dresses is ending.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the six letters of winter, the back three survive the halving.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are terminal points, the final stops or limits of a route, hence ends.

clue.text: Deal with historical complaints of eldest lot working at sixty, say

indicators.note: working implies being put into action and moved about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
sixty is three twenties, an example of scores

explanation.surface: The oldest employees, still working at sixty, have long-standing grievances to air.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so sixty is a number of scores, with 'say' marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle old scores is to take revenge for past wrongs, resolving grudges long held.

clue.text: Compensating quality of South Africa's very popular horse competition

blocks.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
v is the abbreviation for very
in means fashionable
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse
a race is a contest

explanation.surface: South Africa's well-loved horse race has one redeeming feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A saving grace is a redeeming feature that makes up for faults elsewhere.

clue.text: Go wrong up to a certain time on the radio, then sparkle?

indicators.note: what is heard on the radio is only sounds, so the pieces are spelt by ear

blocks.clueFragment: Go wrong up to a certain time
blocks.note: to sin is to go wrong, till means up to, and eight o'clock is a certain time

explanation.surface: A radio presenter goes off the rails until a set hour, then shines.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, 'sin till eight' gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To scintillate is to give off sparks or flashes of light, or figuratively to be brilliantly lively.

clue.text: Empty container within another

indicators.note: within means inside, so one vessel is placed inside the other

blocks.note: a vat is a large container
a can is a container

explanation.surface: An empty box nested within another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another container, which the solver must supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant means unoccupied or containing nothing, so it is a synonym for empty.

clue.text: Ritual of American artist in Hong Kong in front of flag (pointless!)

indicators.note: something in a place is held inside it, so the territory abbreviation goes round
a point is a compass direction letter, so one of those is dropped from the word
placing one part in front of another sets their order left to right

blocks.note: HK is the abbreviation for Hong Kong
A is a standard abbreviation for American
RA is a Royal Academician
the iris, or yellow flag, is a plant

explanation.surface: An American painter in Hong Kong stands before a flag in some pointless ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag here is the plant, not a banner; S (south) is the compass point removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hara-kiri is the Japanese ritual suicide by disembowelment, also called seppuku.

clue.text: Requires massages, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to knead is to massage

explanation.surface: Someone reportedly needs a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to require it; the verb forms match.

clue.text: One favouring what's new, first seen by river in Minnesota

indicators.note: something in a state sits inside its abbreviation
seen by means placed beside, so the pieces sit next to each other

blocks.note: MN is the postal abbreviation for Minnesota
the Oder is a river between Germany and Poland
1st, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A trendsetter is first spotted beside a river in Minnesota.
explanation.definitionFit: A modernist champions modern ideas and styles, rejecting tradition in favour of novelty.

clue.text: Statesmen ordered resources check

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so the letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Politicians commissioned an audit of resources.
explanation.definitionFit: A means test is an assessment of someone's income and assets to decide eligibility for benefits.

clue.text: Criminal damage upset jockey touring area

indicators.note: in a down entry, set upside down means the word is read bottom to top
touring means travelling around, so one word goes round the letter

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil
a jockey is a rider of racehorses
a is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A disgruntled jockey travels around the region doing criminal damage.
explanation.walkthrough: A ram-raider is a British term for a thief who drives a vehicle through a shop front to loot it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram-raider is a type of criminal who smashes in with a car, so it is an example of a criminal.

clue.text: German writer reaching Saxony perhaps (growth area)

blocks.note: Günter Grass, author of The Tin Drum
Saxony is one of Germany's federal states, each called a Land

explanation.surface: A German author arrives in Saxony, which is a growth area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth area' sounds like economics but means a place where grass grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassland is land covered with grasses, so it is literally an area of plant growth.

clue.text: Child's poster work covering course feature

indicators.note: in a down entry, covering means sitting on top, so the earlier pieces come first

blocks.note: an ad, or advertisement, can be a poster
op is short for opus, a work
a tee is found on a golf course

explanation.surface: A child's poster artwork covers a golf course feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An adoptee is a person, typically a child, taken in by adoption.

clue.text: Carry award back for Mr Big?

indicators.note: going back means travelling the reverse way, so the joined words are read right to left

blocks.note: to lug is to carry something heavy
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone carries an award home for the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a powerful magnate, an important person like a Mr Big.

clue.text: Part of craft initially used near winch in strong wind

indicators.note: initially points to the starting letter of each word
something in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a gale is a strong wind
the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Part of a boat's equipment, first used near a winch in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' is a vessel, not a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunwale is the upper edge of a boat's side, a structural part of the vessel.

clue.text: Indication of agreement to accept mail when services are abandoned because of this?

definitions.text: services are abandoned because of this?

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so other letters go inside

blocks.note: ay is an old word for yes
post is mail
as can mean when

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to take the post while church services stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: religious services are abandoned through loss of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostasy is renouncing one's religion, a reason someone would stop attending worship.

clue.text: Section of Hampton garden country

indicators.note: a section is a part cut from a whole, so the letters run inside the words

blocks.note: letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A part of a garden at Hampton is set aside for a national display.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampton Court is a palace near London famous for its gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Polynesian island kingdom in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Setting for Chronicles some Captain rang about

indicators.note: some means just part, so the answer is a run of letters within the words
turning about means facing the other way, so the run is read backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters across the two words, before turning

explanation.surface: A captain phones round about the setting for a historical account.
explanation.walkthrough: Chronicles reads like history or the Bible, but it is C. S. Lewis's Chronicles of Narnia.
explanation.definitionFit: Narnia is the fantasy land in which C. S. Lewis set his seven-novel series.

clue.text: He entertains in house on street

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means sitting above, so that piece comes first

blocks.note: ho is an abbreviation for house
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A man throws parties in his house on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a person who receives and entertains guests.

clue.text: It could give Nice altered tone potentially?

definitions.text: It could give Nice altered tone potentially?

indicators.note: potentially means as it might be, so the letters can become something else

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something might change the mood in the French city of Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a friendly accord with Britain could change the tone in France, where Nice is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Entente Cordiale was the 1904 Anglo-French agreement that improved relations between the two countries.

clue.text: Dad tucked into what's left – of this?

definitions.text: Dad tucked into what's left – of this?

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: the rest is what remains
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Father eats the leftovers of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the answer: leftovers are what remains of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a meal, the thing whose remains a father might tuck into.

clue.text: Workers' representatives meet resistance (crucial) and flop

blocks.note: TU is a trade union
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
key means vitally important

explanation.surface: Union leaders face crucial resistance and their plan fails.
explanation.walkthrough: A turkey is informal for a failure, especially a show or film.
explanation.definitionFit: A turkey is slang for a theatrical or commercial failure, i.e. a flop.
